subject: SET statement
notes: kb/Work PB450 half 2. GR12 - "If identifier-5 is specified, the address identified by identifier-6 is stored in each data item referenced by identifier-5 in the order specified" (cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 OK) - is a rule about a LIST, and the list could not be written: identifier-5 receivers reached Format 7 only through setToValueStatement/setObjectReferenceStatement, where the sender may not be a data-address-identifier, so `SET P1 P2 TO ADDRESS OF REC1` was `COBOL0001` while `SET P1 P2 TO P0` worked. GR12 and GR13 are now ONE loop over ONE receiver list whose elements carry their own kind (BoundSetPointer.Receivers / BoundPointerReceiver), which is how the standard writes them; the separate BoundSetAddressOfBased node that held GR13 at arity one is DELETED, so a mixed statement is expressible at all. The sender is evaluated ONCE (it is one operand OUTSIDE the printed repetition), which ctx.SendOnce already gave the plain route. MEASURED: `SET P1 P2 TO ADDRESS OF REC-A` then rebasing two based items through P1 and P2 gives T1 AAAA AAAA. DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED: GR12's second sentence ("Item identification of the data item referenced by identifier-5 is done immediately before the value of that data item is changed") is observable only through a SUBSCRIPTED identifier-5, and 13.18.60.3 SR14 makes a pointer table unwritable - a USAGE POINTER item may appear only at level 1 or under a STRONG type declaration - so there is no conforming witness and none is faked (measured: `05 PT USAGE POINTER OCCURS 3` draws COBOL1724).
